In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dielectric constant of a solvent is not only dependent on its composition, but also on the nature of the solute.

the dielectric constant of a mixed solvent, in the presence of a solute, is not a function of temperature alone but is also influenced by the nature of the solute and the volume ratio of the mixed solvent.

, in a mixture of water with a weakly protic solvent (methanol, ethanol, glycerol, ethylene glycol, dimethyl sulfoxide) at a given temperature, the dielectric constant of the solution is always higher than that of the solvent and is always lower than the dielectric constant at the same temperature and the same solvent concentration of a solution of the same solvent in water.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dielectric constant is not a constant, but a function of temperature and composition of the solvent.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the dielectric constant of a mixed solvent system, in which water is the dominant component, can be predicted by a linear interpolation of the dielectric constant for the two solvents at the same volume ratio, provided that the temperature is not too low.
